problem.title: What if you could see inside their minds?
problem.bodyOne: Every EAL/D student arrives as a blunt number: a placement score, a stanine, a CEFR band. They progress through broad ACARA phases. None of it gives you empirical insight into their actual linguistic profile.
problem.bodyTwo: So what to teach Monday, who to group with whom, whether your lessons are working, whether they're ready for mainstream. All of it comes down to intuition. What if you had psychometric data to support you?

solution.intro: A diagnostic and progress test built for EAL/D classrooms, Years 7–12.
solution.body: SchoolTest measures 4 skills and 27 subskills across reading, listening, speaking and writing. 30 minutes per skill, showing ACARA progression every time you test.
solution.tagline: Assessment stops being a summary and starts being a map.

Different abilities.

meta.description: What to say and do before, during and after the sitting.

RunSheet.title: Test-day run sheet
RunSheet.subtitle: Everything you need to run the sitting, step by step. Print it out and keep it close by.

before.title: Before the day
before.itemOne: Check your class list ahead of time: every student needs their correct school email to log in. Fix any wrong emails before test day.
before.itemTwo: On the day, open the test-day screen for your class and start a sitting.

start.title: When you start
start.itemOne: Reveal the access code on the test-day screen and write it on the board.
start.itemTwo: Students open the SchoolTest app, enter the code and their school email, and begin.

say.title: What to tell your students
say.intro: Say this to the class before they begin:
say.lineTwo: Each part gets a bit harder, so do not worry if it feels that way.
say.lineThree: If you do not know an answer, have your best guess and move on.
say.lineFour: When the time runs out, the app moves you on by itself.
say.lineFive: Between the parts you can take a moment, and tap continue when you are ready.

during.title: During the test
during.itemOne: Walk the room and supervise as you normally would.
during.itemTwo: The class progress list on the test-day screen shows who has joined, who is working and who has submitted.
during.itemThree: You cannot pause or change the test, and you do not need to start the breaks. Each student taps continue when they are ready.

trouble.title: If something goes wrong
trouble.itemOne: A student who is away sits later. Keep the sitting open or start a new one when they are back, and reveal the code for them.
trouble.itemTwo: If the app crashes or a laptop goes flat, choose Re-sit next to the student's name on the test-day screen. The student joins again with the code and their school email.

after.title: After the test
after.itemOne: When every student has submitted, close the sitting on the test-day screen.
after.itemTwo: Results appear on your dashboard once the scoring has finished.
